chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, who said:
I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the one in i'tikaf who has sexual intercourse. He said: “If he does that, then upon him is what is upon the one who performs zihar.”
And it has also been narrated: “If he has sexual intercourse during the night, then upon him is one expiation; and if he has sexual intercourse during the day, then upon him are two expiations.”

key_terms.اللَّيْلِ: the night period, distinguished here in legal consequence
key_terms.النَّهَارِ: the daytime period, distinguished here in legal consequence
key_terms.الْمُظَاهِرِ: one who has performed zihar and is therefore liable for its expiation
key_terms.الْمُعْتَكِفِ: a person observing i'tikaf, a spiritual retreat in the mosque
key_terms.كَفَّارَةٌ: an expiation required as legal atonement

ai.seo_question: What is the kaffarah for having sexual relations while in i'tikaf?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one in i'tikaf who engages in sexual relations, stating that such a person incurs the expiation of zihar. It also reports a distinction between intercourse at night and during the day, with one expiation for the night and two for the day.
